analysis.title: Q4 2026 Market Outlook: Resilience meets rising risks
key_insights: Eastspring remains constructive on global equities over the short term and has turned positive on US Treasuries on the back of higher bond yields.

3Q review: global equities rose 1.7% on resilient economic growth and earnings, with the US leading developed markets. Global bonds fell 2.5% as heavy sovereign issuance and fiscal deficits pressured longer maturities.
The S&P GSCI Index surged 25.1% and crude oil returned 38.7%, driven by renewed geopolitical tensions and energy outperformance.
The Korean won gained 14.1% against the USD, supported by strong exports and exporters' dollar selling. The USD strengthened marginally overall.
Asia growth is expected to moderate gradually over coming quarters. Robust AI investment should support Asian growth despite higher rates and reduced fiscal support.

Asia inflation is moving above target, though modestly, and higher energy prices are expected to extend price pressures. This pressures Asian central banks to hike, and Asian tightening continues while China diverges.
Lower energy prices and renewed dollar weakness are needed to stabilise monetary policy across Asia.
Eastspring thinks the market may be overpricing Fed hikes. Rate hikes by other G7 central banks may help limit the dollar's upside.
Currency view: the USD is expected to peak soon and weaken in H2 2027.
Key risks are AI, energy and geopolitics. A sharp decline in AI investment combined with another surge in energy prices would disrupt US and Asian growth.
A potential positive catalyst is an earlier Middle East truce, which could lower energy prices and bond yields.
Any new aggression by Russia that expands its conflict beyond Ukraine to a NATO state in Europe would be a major shock to markets.
earnings_insights: Resilient earnings are cited as a driver of the 3Q global equity gain. The report gives no company-level figures.
